skill.name: nano-banana-2
skill.description: Generate and edit images with the inference.sh CLI for Google Gemini image generation. Supports text prompts, image inputs, aspect ratios, resolution settings, multiple images, and Google Search grounding.
skill.summary: Use inference.sh commands to generate and edit Gemini images from prompts and image inputs.
skill.author: tul-sh

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally uses the infsh CLI to call external image-generation services, so several command-use findings are confirmed. Most Ruby backtick detections are Markdown formatting or parameter names and are false positives. No prompt injection attempt was found, but the skill should better constrain CLI permissions and warn about third-party data sharing.

remediation.suggestion: Limit allowed tool patterns to the infsh subcommands required for image generation, sampling, login, and listing.
Add a clear notice that prompts, image URLs, and uploaded images may be sent to inference.sh, Google Gemini, and Google Search grounding.
Move npx skills add examples behind a verification note and recommend reviewing related skills before installation.

content.user_title: Generate Gemini Images with Nano Banana 2
content.value_statement: Image teams need quick access to Gemini image generation and editing from an AI assistant. This skill provides infsh commands for prompts, image inputs, size settings, and Google Search grounding.
actual_capabilities: Runs Gemini image generation through the inference.sh infsh CLI.
Creates images from text prompts with configurable aspect ratios.
Edits existing images by passing image inputs to the model.
Requests multiple images from one prompt when supported by the app.
Uses resolution and output format options documented by the skill.
Shows Google Search grounding for current or factual visual prompts.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and an authenticated account before use.
Sends prompts and image inputs to external inference services.
Model availability, pricing, and quality depend on inference.sh and Google.
The skill documents examples but does not implement local image processing.

use_cases.title: Create campaign visuals
use_cases.description: Generate several concept images with different sizes for ads, social posts, or landing pages.

use_cases.title: Edit source images
use_cases.description: Pass an existing image and ask Gemini to add, remove, or restyle visual elements.

use_cases.title: Prototype visual directions
use_cases.description: Explore prompt styles, lighting, composition, and output settings before a final design pass.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a basic image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Nano Banana 2 to generate one image of [subject] in [style] with [mood].

prompt_templates.title: Create multiple variations
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate four variations of [subject] for [channel]. Use a [ratio] aspect ratio and keep the style consistent.

prompt_templates.title: Edit an existing image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this image input and change [specific element]. Preserve [important details] and output a polished result.

prompt_templates.title: Ground a current scene
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt with Google Search grounding
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a visual scene about [current topic]. Enable Google Search grounding and use a [style] composition for [audience].

output_examples.input: Generate a square product concept image for a reusable water bottle in a studio setting.
output_examples.output: A generated image result with a short model description and metadata about the image request.

output_examples.input: Edit a landscape image by adding a rainbow and warmer sunset lighting.
output_examples.output: An edited image result that keeps the source scene while adding the requested weather and lighting changes.

output_examples.input: Create four logo concepts for a coffee shop with a minimalist style.
output_examples.output: Several generated logo directions that can be compared for style, color, and composition.

best_practices: Confirm that prompts and image inputs can be shared with external services before running the CLI.
Use specific visual details for subject, style, composition, lighting, and output size.
Start with lower resolution drafts, then request higher resolution outputs for selected concepts.
anti_patterns: Do not send confidential images, private documents, or regulated data without approval.
Do not rely on vague prompts when the output needs a specific brand or layout.
Do not install related skills from external sources without reviewing their contents first.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It provides commands and examples for generating or editing images with Gemini through inference.sh.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Do I need an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples require the infsh CLI and login before running image generation.

faq.question: Can it edit existing images?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill shows image editing by passing image inputs with an editing prompt.

faq.question: Can it use current information?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents a Google Search grounding option for current or factual visual prompts.

faq.question: What security review is needed?
faq.answer: Review prompts and image inputs before sharing them, because generation uses external services.
